claim: Apoptosis is an essential physiological process responsible for the elimination and disposal of malignant or excessive cells in multicellular organisms.
source: Apoptosis, a form of programmed cell death, is an essential physiological process responsible for the elimination and disposal of malignant or excessive cells in multicellular organisms (Fuchs and Steller, 2011).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The loss of outer-mitochondrial membrane integrity, known as mitochondrial outer-membrane (MOM) permeabilization (MOMP), is regarded as an irreversible event.
source: The loss of outer-mitochondrial membrane integrity, known as mitochondrial outer-membrane (MOM) permeabilization (MOMP), is regarded as an irreversible event, resulting in the release of cytochrome c and apoptotic factors from the mitochondria that leads to the activation of caspases and cell death (Kale et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: MOMP results in the release of cytochrome c and apoptotic factors from the mitochondria that leads to the activation of caspases and cell death.

claim: MOMP is tightly regulated by BCL-2 protein family proteins, including both pro- and anti-apoptotic regulators that share from one to four homology motifs (BH1 to BH4).

claim: BCL-2 and its anti-apoptotic homologs possess all four BH motifs.
source: BCL-2 and its anti-apoptotic homologs possess all four BH motifs and keep the effector pore-forming multi-BH domain pro-apoptotic proteins, BAX and BAK, from inducing MOMP through direct binary protein-protein interactions (Kale et al., 2018; Bogner et al., 2020).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citations.

claim: AZD-4320 only partially reduced the binding of VPUMA-d26 with CBCL-2.

claim: The primary mechanism of resistance to BH3-mimetics is a 'double-bolt lock', similar to BIM.

claim: 79% of the images of EGFPBIK-L61G expressing cells were classified as showing ER localization.
source: As expected, 79% of the images of EGFPBIK-L61G expressing cells were classified as showing ER localization (yellow bars) compared to 55% for EGFPPUMA-4E (Figure 4A).

claim: Exogenously expressed PUMA localizes to the ER in a BH3-independent, CTS-dependent manner.

claim: When exogenously expressed the PUMA CTS localizes the protein primarily to the ER.

claim: Incremental deletions of the PUMA CTS decreased the Pearson's correlation coefficient of the mutant proteins with ER localization.
source: Incremental deletions of the PUMA CTS decreased the Pearson's correlation coefficient of the mutant proteins with ER localization suggesting that deleting as few as the last 11 amino acids (VPUMA-d11) impacts ER localization (Figure 4D).

claim: The entire CTS contributes to PUMA localization.
source: As progressive deletion of the CTS correlated with decreasing ER localization, this suggests that the entire CTS contributes to PUMA localization.
evidence: This is an inference based on data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The fusion protein with Venus at the C-terminus of PUMA (PUMAV) retained ER localization.
source: Unexpectedly, the fusion protein with Venus at the C-terminus of PUMA (PUMAV) retained ER localization (Figure 4C and D), suggesting that unlike CTS of BIK which fully inserts into the ER (Wilfling et al., 2012) the CTS of PUMA is not a conventional tail-anchor that spans the membrane bilayer.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figures 4C and 4D.

claim: The CTS of PUMA is not a conventional tail-anchor that spans the membrane bilayer.
source: Unexpectedly, the fusion protein with Venus at the C-terminus of PUMA (PUMAV) retained ER localization (Figure 4C and D), suggesting that unlike CTS of BIK which fully inserts into the ER (Wilfling et al., 2012) the CTS of PUMA is not a conventional tail-anchor that spans the membrane bilayer.

claim: Both PUMA and PUMA-d26 bind to BCL-XL at both the ER and the mitochondria.

claim: Endogenous PUMA co-localized more with the mitochondrial landmark (ChActA) (Pearson correlation coefficient ≈ 0.6) than the ER landmark (ChCb5) (Pearson correlation coefficient ≈ 0.4) in MCF-7 cells.

claim: An increase in Pearson correlation coefficients for PUMA to both the ER and the mitochondria was observed at the highest concentrations of Thapsigargin, Tunicamycin, and Etoposide.
source: Intriguingly, we saw an increase in Pearson correlation coefficients for PUMA to both the ER and the mitochondria, most notably at the highest concentrations of the 3 drugs (Figure 4—figure supplement 3C).

claim: PUMA subcellular localization in living cells is dynamic and dependent not only on the inherent specificity of the PUMA CTS but also on the abundance and localization of its binding partners.

claim: Both VPUMA-d26-ER1 and VPUMA-d26-ER2 bound to CBCL-XL in a BH3-dependent manner in BMK-dko cells.
